llmAccess.gatewayAuthNote: Auth: during testing (server without NEXOS_ADMIN_TOKEN) no Authorization header is needed and admin is assumed; production requires Authorization: Bearer <admin token> (set in Settings → API Token).
llmAccess.reasoningNote: The response contains a reasoning field: thinking models such as Qwen reason before answering — an empty or null content with non-empty reasoning is normal, not a failure.
llmAccess.respReasoningSample: Reasoning (thinking models reason first; empty string when none)
llmAccess.launchNote: Full vllm serve command: for spawned instances this is the most recent real command (with the venv binary path); otherwise it is constructed from the current config. Copy to reproduce.

gatewayAccess.sec1Title: ① Access Token (the key the AI needs)
gatewayAccess.keyNone: No token generated/pasted yet — the access block will use a placeholder (unusable for the AI)
gatewayAccess.genTokenNote: One click creates a free-mode token (agent-access-<date>, unmetered & unlimited — AI trial calls never hit a quota wall; for metered use create a per_token token in the Tokens tab). The full key is shown only in the creation response and is merged into the access block below automatically.
gatewayAccess.keyInput: Or paste an existing token's full key (sk-os-…)
gatewayAccess.pasteHint: The token list only shows masked keys — an existing token's full key is visible only at creation; if you can't find it, just generate a new one above.
gatewayAccess.blockSecTitle: ② One-click access block (paste to an AI and it can start calling)
gatewayAccess.blockHint: Copy the whole block below to any AI assistant / agent / tool: it contains the Base URL, API Key, available models and two curl + OpenAI SDK examples — the AI can call directly with it.
gatewayAccess.perModelTitle: Per-model copy (compact block: URL + key + single-model curl)
gatewayAccess.streamNote: Streaming responses are text/event-stream, forwarded chunk by chunk; billing uses the usage reported by the upstream in the final chunk (send stream_options.include_usage; if absent it is recorded as 0 and noted in the call log).
gatewayAccess.baseUrlHint: Use 127.0.0.1 for local access; use the node IP from other machines (gateway listens on 0.0.0.0:{port}).
gatewayAccess.authNote: Every call carries Authorization: Bearer <gateway token> (sk-os- prefix). The token IS the quota: billing mode and whitelists are set at creation, usage is deducted in real time.
gatewayAccess.tokenContract: Create token contract (POST /api/v1/gateway/tokens, admin auth required)
gatewayAccess.adminNote: "Generate access token" calls an admin write endpoint: in the test period (server without NEXOS_AUTH_DEFAULT_ADMIN=0) credential-less requests are treated as admin; on deployments with an admin token configured, fill it in Settings → API token first or generation returns 401.
gatewayAccess.billingFree: free: no metering, no charge (quota shows ∞)
gatewayAccess.billingPerToken: per_token: charged per upstream token usage (default)
gatewayAccess.billingImage: per_image: fixed credits per generated image
gatewayAccess.billingCredits: credits: prepaid credit pool, all usage deducts credits
gatewayAccess.quotaNote: Exhausted quota returns 429 (rejected when quota_used ≥ quota_limit; free skips the check). Credits can be topped up via payment orders / redeem codes.
gatewayAccess.whitelistNote: Whitelists: allowed_models restricts models the token may call, allowed_channels restricts routable channels (empty = unrestricted); calling a non-whitelisted model returns 403.
gatewayAccess.failoverNote: Failover: channels are tried by priority; streaming requests only fail over before the first byte (no switching after chunks started, to avoid splicing streams).
gatewayAccess.genTokenDone: Token generated; the full key is merged into the access block (shown once; the copy block carries the full text)
gatewayAccess.genTokenNoKey: Token created but the response carried no full key (backend issue? copy it manually from the creation response)
gatewayAccess.lanShareTitle: Share federated models on the LAN (relay channels)
gatewayAccess.lanShareNote: Federated APIs consumed via P2P (the 🌐 relay entries in External APIs) can be published to the gateway as relay channels in one click: APIs received over P2P are re-published to AI tools on this LAN by this node’s gateway — the integration surface stays exactly the same.
gatewayAccess.lanShareStep1: Click “Publish to Gateway” on the External APIs card (or pick an entry under “Add channel → Import from External API”);
gatewayAccess.lanShareStep2: LAN AI tools point at the same Base URL + this node’s token (sk-os-); requests to relay channels are forwarded by the source node via the overlay;
gatewayAccess.lanShareStep3: Local auth/billing/logs work as usual (node autonomy); relay failures fail over to other channels by priority.
gatewayAccess.lanShareTrust: Trust chain: holder of this node’s token → via this node → URLs within the source node’s allowlist (the source only forwards its own published entries — never an open proxy).

netboot.title: 🌐 Network Install (USB iPXE → type this node's IP → fully automatic Ubuntu + cluster join)
netboot.subtitle: Install Ubuntu Server on any bare-metal machine and join the NexOS cluster automatically: burn the USB once (official ipxe.iso); versions, menus and seeds always come from this node. LAN only, no Internet required.
netboot.step1Desc: Download the official ipxe.iso on the right (~9.4MB, BIOS+UEFI), write it to a USB stick with balenaEtcher / dd / Ventoy.
netboot.step2Desc: Boot from the USB (disable Secure Boot on UEFI machines). iPXE runs DHCP then asks for the NexOS server IP — press Enter to accept the default source IP, or type this node's IP.
netboot.step3Desc: The menu lists the latest stable Ubuntu Server in the repo. It fetches kernel/ISO, installs via autoinstall unattended (whole disk wiped!), then runs install.sh to join the cluster (default account nexos/nexos — change on first login).
netboot.usbTitle: USB stick creation (pick one of three)
netboot.usbDesc: All three methods produce the same result; pick a BIOS/legacy boot entry if the machine lacks UEFI.
netboot.usbCommands:
# Method 1: balenaEtcher (GUI, simplest)
#   Etcher → Flash from file → ipxe.iso → Flash to USB

# Method 2: dd (Linux/macOS, replace /dev/sdX with your stick)
sudo dd if=ipxe.iso of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress oflag=direct

# Method 3: Ventoy (multi-ISO library)
#   Install Ventoy on the stick → copy ipxe.iso onto it → pick it at boot
netboot.usbNote: Note: machines with Secure Boot enabled cannot boot the unsigned iPXE — disable Secure Boot in BIOS/UEFI settings first. The Clonezilla entry in the menu is a P1 placeholder.
netboot.rollPolicy: Version policy = rolling latest-stable only: add the new release → Delete the old one. Older versions (e.g. 24.04) are not offered by the automatic flow; manually placed ISOs remain available for manual installs.
netboot.repoEmpty: Repo is empty: drop ubuntu-*-live-server-*.iso into the repo directory and press Scan (sha256 verification and boot-file extraction run in the background).
netboot.confirmDelete: Delete {file} from the repo (with sidecar and extracted boot files)? This is the rolling-policy remove-old operation.
netboot.backgroundHint: sha256 verification / boot-file extraction running in background; refreshes automatically…

llmInst.paramsSub: Launch parameters configurable when creating an instance, to help you decide when to tune them.
llmInst.paramTp1: Tensor parallelism: splits the model across GPUs. Default 1 (single card). Increase with multiple identical GPUs to use all VRAM
llmInst.paramTp2: (e.g. 2 for two cards). Note multi-card adds communication overhead — bigger is not always better.
llmInst.paramGmu1: Fraction of GPU VRAM vLLM may use, 0~1, default 0.9. Larger fits longer contexts / bigger KV cache
llmInst.paramGmu2: but may affect other processes on the same card. Lower it (e.g. 0.5) when VRAM is tight or shared with other GPU tasks.
llmInst.paramMml1: Maximum context length in tokens, default 8192. Larger allows longer input+output but increases VRAM usage,
llmInst.paramMml2: bounded by both the model's context limit and available VRAM.
llmInst.paramQuant1: Quantization: None / awq / gptq. Quantized models use less VRAM and can run larger models, but lose
llmInst.paramQuant2: a little precision. Set only when the model itself is a quantized build.
llmInst.paramDtype1: Compute dtype: auto (by hardware) / float16 / bfloat16. auto works for most cases. Newer cards (A100/
llmInst.paramDtype2: H100/RTX 30+) prefer bfloat16 for stability; older cards may not support bf16 — use float16.
llmInst.paramSmn1: Model name exposed via the API (the model field of OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions). Defaults to
llmInst.paramSmn2: model. An alias decouples clients from the real model path.
llmInst.paramTrust1: Whether to allow running custom Python code from the model repo (often required by Qwen/GLM etc.). Security risk —
llmInst.paramTrust2: enable only for models from trusted sources.

exit.title: WAN Exit
exit.disabledA: Exit sharing relies on the P2P overlay (encrypted direct / hole-punch / relay). Set
exit.disabledB: and restart os-api: this node can then offer its exit to others, and traffic can egress via other exit nodes (local SOCKS5).

exit.socksSub: Point your browser/system proxy here (SOCKS5) to egress via the default exit
exit.defaultSetOk: Default exit = {id} — point browser/system proxy to {addr} to egress through it
exit.authEmpty: No authorizations (other nodes cannot egress via this node by default)
exit.useSub: Exit offers learned via metadata exchange (exit_offered)
exit.useEmpty: No exit nodes discovered yet — once a peer offers its exit in Network, it appears after 1-2 metadata rounds

p2p.title: P2P Network
p2p.disabledA: The fully distributed Kademlia overlay (peer discovery / encrypted links / NAT hole-punching / relay) is off by default. Set
p2p.disabledB: and restart: this machine becomes a peer node (optionally
p2p.disabledD: to declare a public service role).
p2p.conflictTitle: ⚠️ Same public key seen from {n} addresses
p2p.conflictNote: Multiple OSes sharing one private key share permissions (identity = key, by design); files of different OSes do not sync. Local notice only — connections and messages are not blocked.
p2p.empty: No known peers yet (point NEXOS_P2P_BOOTSTRAP at an anchor, or wait for LAN mDNS discovery).
p2p.bucketAria: k-bucket usage bar chart (160 buckets in 16 segments)
p2p.sendToPh: Target NodeID (0x…66 hex, copy from the table above)
p2p.sendErr: Fill in target NodeID and message body
